behavior: A ground-foraging plover that runs rapidly, pauses to watch and listen, then pecks or pulls invertebrates from sand or mud. Migrants and nonbreeding birds often forage and roost in flocks; breeding birds are territorial and perform slow, exaggerated display flights.
field_marks: Chunky, large-headed profile with a short neck
Short, thick black bill and large dark eye
Breeding plumage has a black face and belly bordered by white
Upperparts are strongly checkered or mottled black, white, gray, and brown
Long, pointed wings; short, mostly whitish tail and diagnostic black axillaries visible in flight
habitat: Breeds on open wet or dry Arctic tundra. During migration it uses coastlines, muddy lake and river margins, wet fields, and short grasslands; nonbreeding habitat includes mudflats, tidal flats, beaches, estuaries, lagoons, and salt marshes.
